items.t: Why Ukraine’s defense industry may have hit a ceiling
items.m: Ukraine’s defense industry fell apart after the Soviet Union collapsed, and by the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion, the country made almost no weapons of its own. After the invasion, however, the sector grew rapidly, largely thanks to European funding. That growth has let Ukraine keep fighting even as U.S. support has shrunk and the European Union has been unable to supply enough weapons.

items.t: Zelenskiy says intelligence shows Russia planning new strikes on Ukraine
items.m: Nov 23 - Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday that intelligence showed Russia planned new strikes on Ukraine, and he urged the United States and other countries to take note as supplies of air defence systems depended on their decisions.

items.t: Moscow accuses Estonia of hostile actions on 'verge of triggering open war'

items.t: German-Ukrainian interceptor shoots down Russian jet-powered drone, company says
items.m: The GUR, Ukraine's military intelligence agency, said Russian forces began using the K5-K variant of the Geran-5 drone in attacks on Ukrainian cities at the beginning of autumn.

items.t: Russia protests Estonia’s planned land border closure and again accuses it of letting Ukrainian drones use its airspace
items.m: Russia’s Foreign Ministry summoned Estonia’s acting chargé d’affaires in Moscow, Marek Juhtegi, and lodged a “strong protest” over Estonia’s accusation that Moscow tried to set fire to a defense plant and the Estonian government’s decision to close the border with Russia.

items.t: Russia’s statistics agency listed heart disease as the cause of Ukrainian journalist Viktoriia Roshchyna’s death in Russian custody, leaked records show
items.m: Official Russian documents attribute Ukrainian journalist Viktoriia Roshchyna’s death in Russian custody to heart disease and pulmonary edema. BBC News Russian, Verstka, and iStories reported the finding after reviewing leaked data from Rosstat, Russia’s federal statistics agency.

items.t: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz says it was a mistake to leave Ukraine out of NATO in 2008
items.m: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Ukraine should have been admitted to NATO in 2008. He made the remarks at a joint press conference with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, Die Zeit reported.

items.t: How Ukraine destroyed one of Russia's newest warships
items.m: Ukraine says its naval drones sank one of Russia's newest vessels – the corvette Merkury – in a Libyan port. Seven drones were used in the attack, which also hit a cargo ship which President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia used to transport weapons. CBC's Briar Stewart explains what we know about the operation.

items.t: 'A war of unmanned machines, AI and total transparency of the battlefield'
items.m: Speaking with FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney, Nobel Peace Prize laureate Oleksandra Matviichuk, Director of the Centre for Civil Liberties, says that today's war in Ukraine "is a war of unmanned machines, AI, total transparency of the battlefield, mass drones attacks and long range weapons, and this means we have to rethink how to protect human beings".

items.t: Russian news agencies and TV channels ignore Ukraine’s sinking of a Russian warship off the Libyan coast
items.m: Russian news agencies and state TV channels chose not to report on the Merkuriy, a corvette sunk by Ukrainian forces in Libya.

items.t: Estonia’s interior minister suggests petitioning Putin to end war in Ukraine after Narva resident launches petition to keep border with Russia open for family visits
items.m: Ksenia Agar, a Narva resident, has launched a petition asking Estonia to keep its border with Russia open for family visits.

items.t: NATO warns Putin could strike before European army responds, points to US as military model
items.m: NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte warned Russia's war machine runs at full speed and could threaten Europe long after the war in Ukraine ends.

items.m: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is calling for a new round of negotiations involving Ukraine, Russia, the United States and European leaders, saying Kyiv is ready to meet as early as Tuesday.

items.t: Ukraine’s drone strike on Russian warship in Libya risks ‘serious escalation,’ former official warns
items.m: Morgan Murphy warned the Ukrainian sea drone strike on the Russian corvette Mercury in Benghazi risks a serious escalation of the nearly five-year war.

items.t: Ukraine sinks Russian warships thousands of miles from battlefield near Libya
items.m: Military video posted by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is said to show the country's naval drone attacks on Russian ships near Libya, thousands of miles from the battlefield. Charlie D'Agata reports.

items.t: Peace in Ukraine won’t end Russian sabotage in Europe, Poland warns
items.m: Poland’s intelligence minister says Moscow's hybrid campaign against Europe could persist whether the war goes Russia’s way or not.

items.t: Hacked Russian data suggests nearly 500,000 soldiers dead, reports say
items.m: Data allegedly stolen by hackers from Russia’s statistics agency Rosstat show the number of recorded Russian military dead is approaching 500,000, several Russian media outlets and German news magazine Der Spiegel reported on Monday. The outlets said they had gained access to the data set, which the hacker groups Cyberpartisans and Silent Crow are said to have taken in an attack on the agency. Reports say the groups are close to the Belarusian opposition or to pro-Ukrainian collectives. Rosstat...

items.t: Russia claims strikes on Starlink terminals, drone sites in Ukraine's Sumy
items.m: Russia's military conducted attacks on military sites in Ukraine's Sumy region using drones and missile strikes. In a separate incident, an overnight attack in Zaporizhzhia resulted in injuries to 11 individuals, including severe cases. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy issued warnings about impending Russian strike preparations while urging increased military aid from allies. He emphasized the importance of anti-ballistic missile systems for Ukraine's defense against aggression.

items.t: Russian attack kills 2 people, wounds 22 in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia, official says
items.m: Nov 24 - A Russian attack killed 2 people and injured 22 more, including 2 children, in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia overnight, Ivan Fedorov, co-head of the Zaporizhzhia Regional Defense Council, said on Telegram on Tuesday.

items.t: Inside the Ukrainian Attack That Sank Russian Warship Docked in Libya

items.t: Live: Tripoli demands explanation from Kyiv for striking Russian ships in Libyan waters
items.m: The Tripoli-based Libyan foreign ministry on Monday condemned a Ukrainian drone attack on two Russian ships near the eastern city of Benghazi over the weekend, demanding an explanation from Kyiv. Meanwhile, South Korean authorities said Tuesday several Russian military aircraft had breached its air defence zone, correcting an earlier alert that reported a North Korean plane had made an incursion. Follow our liveblog for all the latest updates.

items.t: US defense chief has yet to approve Patriot missiles already allocated to Ukraine, FT reports
items.m: Nov 24 - US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has yet to approve the transfer of about 60 Patriot air defence interceptors that Washington had already agreed to supply to Ukraine, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter.

items.t: ICG: "It's hard to imagine" Tripoli would risk its ties with Russia by approving a Ukrainian attack
items.m: Angela Diffley is pleased to welcome Claudia Gazzini, International Crisis Group's Senior Analyst for Libya. The Ukrainian attack on a Russian warship off the coast of eastern Libya has raised questions about Russian and Ukrainian military activity in the country. Gazzini discusses Russia's established military presence in eastern Libya and allegations that Ukrainian forces are operating in the west. items.t: North Korea threatens to shut Swiss office over Russian youth camp sanctions
items.m: North Korea threatened on Tuesday to close a Swiss diplomatic office that opened in Pyongyang last month, condemning Switzerland for imposing sanctions on a youth camp in eastern North Korea over its alleged role in the transfer of children from Russia-occupied areas of Ukraine. Kim Yo-jong, the powerful sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, described the Swiss sanctions on the Songdowon International Children’s Camp in the coastal city of Wonsan as an “open hostile act” and a “serious...

items.t: 355 Ukrainian drones flew toward Moscow overnight, prompting flight restrictions at two airports
items.m: Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 355 Ukrainian drones flew toward the capital overnight on November 24. Air defense forces shot down most of the drones “at distant approaches” and destroyed 63 more as they approached Moscow, he said on his Telegram channel.

items.t: Russian strikes kill two in Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia, injure dozens
items.m: Russian forces struck Zaporizhzhia overnight on November 24, killing two people, said Mykhailo Semikin, the acting head of the regional military administration.

items.t: EU proposes banning Russian athletes from competing in sports events
items.m: 'Sports events cannot be a forum for propaganda activities,' stated EU chief Ursula von der Leyen as the bloc readies its 22nd sanction package in response to Moscow's war in Ukraine.

items.t: Russian drone briefly enters Polish airspace, minister says
items.m: Nov 24 - A Russian drone briefly entered Polish airspace during an attack on neighbouring Ukraine overnight, Poland's military said on Tuesday, an incursion the deputy defence minister said he assumed was a deliberate act.

items.t: Russia says it shot down nearly 700 Ukrainian drones overnight, including 355 targeting Moscow region
items.m: Russia said its air defences intercepted 699 Ukrainian drones overnight, including 355 launched towards the Moscow region.

items.m: Vladyslav Vlasiuk, Ukraine's sanctions commissioner, voiced disappointment over the decision to leave Irish-made alumina out of the latest EU sanctions package against Russia.

items.t: Russia to build Kaliningrad exclave rail ferries, citing transport 'blockade'
items.m: The ferries, due in 2030 and costing around 50 billion roubles, will run between Baltiysk and Ust-Luga and be built in occupied Crimea. Most freight to Kaliningrad has already moved to sea routes, since Lithuania and Poland restricted transit after the 2022 invasion.

items.t: Fighting between Russia and Ukraine has expanded geographically, drawing concerns
items.m: In recent days, Ukraine has sunk a Russian warship docked in port in Libya, and Russian missiles have landed in Poland. The Kremlin has not commented on the missiles.

items.t: Norway and Ukraine to expand cooperation on anti-drone system
items.m: OSLO, Nov 24 - Norway and Ukraine will expand their cooperation on a newly developed anti-drone air defence system, the Norwegian defence ministry said in a statement on Tuesday.

items.t: Lithuanian SIM cards found in Russian drones that attacked Ukraine
items.m: Lithuanian prepaid SIM cards have been found in Russian drones that attacked Ukraine in 2025, the Lithuanian outlet 15 min reported, citing data from Ukrainian military intelligence. The 15 min article is behind a paywall; it was summarized by Delfi and LRT.

items.m: Latvian President Edgars Rinkevics does not believe Moscow was genuinely interested in ending the war.

items.t: Hungarian prime minister set to meet Zelenskiy in western Ukraine on Tuesday
items.m: BUDAPEST, Nov 24 - Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar said he would meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy and leaders of the ethnic Hungarian minority in western Ukraine later on Tuesday, after both countries pledged to improve mutual relations.

items.m: OSLO, Nov 24 - Norway's Defence Minister Tore Sandvik said on Tuesday that there is an ongoing dialogue with Ukraine regarding \"a need for stability in our near areas\".

During the conversation, Tajani stressed the need to respect Libya's sovereignty and not to extend the Ukraine war, the sources said. (ANSA). Read article...

items.t: Narrow majority of Germans oppose military aid to Ukraine in survey
items.m: Nov 24 - A narrow majority of Germans oppose giving military aid to Kyiv as Russia wages war in Ukraine, a reversal from a year ago, according to a survey published by the nonprofit organisation Koerber Stiftung on Tuesday.

items.t: Is North Korea holding back on sending Russia more troops?
items.m: A North Korean troop buildup Ukraine warned about months ago has yet to materialize, even as strategic cooperation continues. Analysts say Pyongyang is balancing its ties with Moscow and Beijing.

items.t: Red lines, political horse-trading and Ukraine: Inside the EU's increasingly bitter budget battle
items.m: EU capitals are divided on several fronts ahead of key talks on the bloc's next long-term budget: overall size, political priorities, Ukraine financing and new EU taxes. Tense domestic politics make compromise harder, with only leaders expected to break the deadlock.

items.t: Russian governor suspected of orchestrating scheme to embezzle and funnel a billion rubles abroad reportedly offers to resign and fight in Ukraine
items.m: The Meshchansky Court in Moscow will soon rule on a pretrial restriction for Andrey Chibis, the governor of the Murmansk region, the Russian business news outlet RBC and the Russian business daily Kommersant reported, citing sources. Investigators plan to seek his arrest, according to the outlets.

items.t: UK bought fake C4 explosives for Ukraine, FT investigation finds
items.m: Britain has for several years bought tons of explosives for Ukraine from an American company that marketed the product as an improved version of the military explosive C4, a Financial Times investigation found. However, tests later showed the material contained no RDX, the key component of standard C4.

items.t: Merz to meet Pope Leo, Meloni in Rome

items.t: Ukraine insists attack on Russian ships in Libya was self-defence
items.m: KYIV, Nov 24 - Ukraine's foreign minister said on Tuesday a drone attack against a Russian military vessel and cargo ship in Libyan waters at the weekend was a legitimate act of self-defence, following criticism from the government in Tripoli.

items.t: UK warns of Russian sabotage threat to companies that supply Ukraine
items.m: LONDON, Nov 24 - Britain's defence ministry and domestic spy agency MI5 on Tuesday issued a warning to companies providing direct support to Ukraine's military that they faced an increased sabotage threat from Russia.
